Subject: Launchpad AI — dedicated GPU pool alignment & operational plan

Hi Eli / Sarah,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the candid routing of the challenges you're seeing in prod. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:￼

Key pain points you described
- Tail latency variability on large embed/generation endpoints during morning batch jobs (spikes up to 2–3x baseline).
- Regulatory requirement to isolate certain model runs and customer data (PCI-adjacent workflows) into a private pool.
- Procurement and forecast uncertainty — you need a clear sizing + pricing recommendation for your upcoming Q4 ramp.

Goals we heard
- Stable p50/p95 latency for interactive endpoints (target p95 <= 250ms for 128-token runs) with healthy headroom for batch windows.
- Fully isolated reserved pool for regulated workloads with customer-managed KMS + audit logs.
- Defined canary / fallback policy for traffic surges and a clear SLA for availability and degradation modes.

Our recommended starting design
1) Dedicated reserved pool: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (can be a mix of A10/A100 depending on availability) sized for your current 95th percentile throughput with 30% headroom for Q4. See attached sizing workbook for the calculation and knobs.
2) Isolation model: single-tenant pool with network ACLs and optional VPC peering; KMS integration point for keys used in model inference.
3) Autoscale + burst: configured burst capacity (up to +50%) for short windows with automatic fallback to a lower-cost compatible model variant if capacity exhausted.
4) SLA targets: 99.5% uptime for the reserved pool; per-request latency SLOs as above with an operational runbook for mitigation and fallback.

Open questions for your team (action items)
- Confirm regulated workload volume (attachments column B in sizing file) — Eli, can you paste the monthly concurrent job numbers for those customer groups?
- Procurement cadence: Marissa, can you share standard PO lead time expectations so we can align billing start date?
- Security: do you require HSM-backed KMS or is cloud KMS acceptable for now?

Attachments and links
- Launchpad_GPU_Sizing_v1.xlsx (sizing assumptions, sensitivity table)
- launchpad_sla_draft_v2.docx (draft SLA with proposed credits & maintenance windows)
- HubSpot deal created: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543

Next steps
1) Launchpad to confirm regulated workload concurrency and procurement lead time (Eli / James) — target by Tue, Sep 14.
2) Redwood to deliver a formal quote and contractual SLA based on confirmed numbers — target by Thu, Sep 16.
3) Book a technical deep-dive (SE + infra) to walk through network/KMS requirements — propose Wed, Sep 15 10:00am PT.

If that aligns, I'll follow up with a calendar invite including Ben (SE) and Marissa (ops). Thanks — excited to get this scoped so we can lock a Q4 go-live.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — this is a great summary and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side:￼

1) Regulated workload volume: preliminary numbers attached below. We're looking at roughly 120 concurrent regulated inference jobs during peak (each ~90–150 tokens). I'll paste the row from the sizing sheet into the drive folder later today.
2) Procurement: typical PO lead time is 3–4 weeks for signed commitments; finance will require the SLA and final quote to approve. James will coordinate.
3) KMS: for the top-tier regulated customers we need HSM-backed keys; for the rest cloud KMS is fine.

On latency — the p95 <= 250ms target is reasonable for interactive endpoints. For some of our heavier generation jobs we accept higher latency but we'd like visibility (tracing/observability) into token-level cost and KV cache hits.

Can we get an initial quote that separates the reserved pool cost from the optional burst capacity and the managed KMS/HSM add-on? That will help procurement compare line items.

Confirming the Sep 15 10:00am PT technical deep-dive works for Ben and your infra folks.

Eli

Eli / team — quick technical notes ahead of Wed's deep-dive:￼

Sizing rationale (short)
- The 8-GPU starting point assumes model mix of two medium-large encoder-decoder models with average token lengths 64–128 and a steady-state concurrency of ~40 requests/sec during peak. The sizing workbook includes a sensitivity tab showing how concurrency maps to GPU count.

Isolation & KMS
- HSM-backed keys: we can support both HSM and cloud KMS. HSM option adds an integration window (we'll run a keywrap flow + attestation) and a small operational lead time; we'll document that in the runbook.
- Network isolation: VPC peering + strict egress ACLs recommended; we can supply Terraform snippets for the setup.

Autoscale & burst policy
- We'll propose a burst pool configured as ephemeral capacity for short jobs (<= 5 min). If burst consumed, traffic routes to a fallback model (quantized variant) — minimal code changes required from your side.

Observability
- We'll enable token-level cost breakdown and KV cache hit/miss metrics in the Console. For compliance customers we can push audit logs to your S3 bucket (or GCS) with daily retention exports.

I'll bring the sizing workbook and a short runbook to the Wed call. If you want, I can also attach example Terraform templates beforehand.

—Ben
